topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning outcomes of the lecture.

topics.label: Foundations of cancer etiology: genetics, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer causation by examining the interplay between intrinsic genetic predisposition, random mutations, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens contribute to oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed mechanistic case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how environmental agents and radiation induce DNA damage directly or via host metabolic activation into reactive compounds.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, microenvironment, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic tumour promoters, chronic inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental stages of host tissues facilitate cancer development.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine carcinogenicity and assess associated risks.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the final summary points and concludes the lecture.
